Per the project's stored release convention (nothing in the repo's docs or CI config contradicts it, though I found no release docs or workflow files to confirm it):

1. Make sure everything you want released is merged to `main`.
2. Push a git tag of the form `vYYYY.MM.N` on `main`. `N` is the release number within that month. For example, `v2026.09.2` would be the second release in September 2026. Today is 2026-10-01, so the first October release would be `v2026.10.1`.

   ```
   git checkout main && git pull
   git tag v2026.10.1
   git push origin v2026.10.1
   ```
3. CI then builds the artifacts, runs the full test suite and publishes the release.

Don't publish packages by hand. Releases are automated end to end.

I didn't find any CI config in the repo, so I can't confirm the pipeline details. If you want, I can check for the latest existing tag to work out the next `N`.
